[[File:Iovitzu Popescu lecturing 1982.jpg|thumb|right|Ioan-Iovitz Popescu giving a lecture, University of Bucharest, 1982]]
'''Ioan-Iovitz "Iovitzu" Popescu''' (October 1, 1932 – 22 December, 2023) was a [[Romania]]n physicist and linguist, emeritus professor at [[University of Bucharest]], Faculty of Physics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fizica.unibuc.ro/Fizica/Prezentare/Cadre/Main.php?Lang=En|title=Staff of University of Bucharest, Faculty of Physics|access-date=2017-03-29|archive-date=2017-07-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730223634/http://www.fizica.unibuc.ro/Fizica/Prezentare/Cadre/Main.php?Lang=En|url-status=dead}}</ref> and member of the [[Romanian Academy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://acad.ro/membri/|title=Members of the Romanian Academy}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acad.ro/sectii/sectia04_fizica/fiz_membri.htm|title=Members of the Romanian Academy, Physical Sciences section}}</ref> In the field of physics, he is best known for his work on [[Electric discharge in gases|gas discharges]] and [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]], as well as his collaborations with Denisa Popescu in [[laser spectroscopy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iipopescu.com/DENISA_POPESCU.html?Lang=En|title=Heralding Laser Spectroscopy - Dr. Denisa-Georgeta Popescu}}</ref> He also had pioneering contributions in the field of [[gamma-ray laser]]s with [[hafnium controversy|Carl B. Collins]] and Silviu Olariu.<ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=nucl-ex/9907010 |title=Amplification of Gamma Radiation from X-Ray Excited Nuclear States|journal=Revue Roumaine de Physique|page=559|volume=27|last1=Olariu|first1=S.|last2=Popescu|first2=I. Iovitzu|last3=Collins|first3=C. B.|year=1982}}</ref>

As of 2006, the focus of Iovitzu Popescu's work had shifted towards the field of [[linguistics]], in cooperation with leading linguist [[Gabriel Altmann]].

== Early life ==
Iovitzu Popescu was born in [[Burila Mare]] village, [[Mehedinți County]]. He is the son of Dumitru Popescu and Elvira (''née'' Iovitz). In 1951 he graduated from [[Traian National College|Traian High School]] in [[Turnu Severin]]. Between 1951 and 1955 he was a student at the University of Bucharest, Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, from which he graduated in 1955 with the thesis "Sodium-Vapor Lamp", supervised by [[Radu Grigorovici]].

== Career ==
In 1955, following graduation, Iovitzu Popescu was offered a position at the University of Bucharest by [[Eugen Bădărău]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iipopescu.com/badareu.htm?Lang=En|title=The works and the school of Eugen Badareu}}</ref> in the Department of Optics and Gas Discharges, which he accepted. In 1961, he obtained his Ph.D. on a thesis entitled "The mechanism of cathodic parts of glow discharges", under Bădărău's supervision.

Between 1960 and 1972 Iovitzu Popescu was head of the Plasma Physics Laboratory at the Institute of Physics, Bucharest. In 1969, he co-authored one of the first experimental studies on nano-clustering in high pressure gases.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Popescu |first1=Iovitzu |last2=von der Heide |first2=Rüdiger |date=1969 |title=Beweglichkeit von Einfach- und Cluster-Ionen in Argon bei hohen Drucken |journal=Zeitschrift für Physik A |language=de |volume=220 |issue=4 |pages=337–348 |doi=10.1007/BF01395619 |bibcode=1969ZPhy..220..337P |s2cid=116142120 |issn=0939-7922}}</ref> From 1967 to 1969 he was a Humboldt fellow at [[University of Kiel]], [[Germany]]. He worked on [[atomic spectroscopy]] with Walter Lochte-Holtgreven and Johannes Richter. In 1970, he started his collaboration with Carl B. Collins, head of the Center for Quantum Electronics at [[University of Texas at Dallas]], on multiphoton spectroscopy and induced gamma emission. In 1974, they co-authored the first experimental report on multiphoton spectra.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Popescu |first1=D. |last2=Collins |first2=C. B. |last3=Johnson |first3=B. W. |last4=Popescu |first4=Iovitzu |date=1974 |title=Multiphoton excitation and ionization of atomic cesium with a tunable dye laser |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.9.1182 |journal=[[Physical Review A]] |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=1182–1187 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.9.1182|bibcode=1974PhRvA...9.1182P |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1972, Popescu became a tenured professor at University of Bucharest, Faculty of Physics. He was the Dean of the Faculty of Physics from 1972 to 1977. Between 1977 and 1981 he headed the newly founded Institute of Physics and Technology of Radiation Devices.

In May 1981, Popescu became [[Rector (academia)|Rector]] of the University of Bucharest, a position he held until October 1989. In 1990 he was elected a titular member of the [[Romanian Academy]], having been a corresponding member for 16 years. He presided over the Physical Sciences Section of the Romanian Academy between 1990 and 1992.

In 1982, Iovitzu Popescu wrote that the [[Aether theories|aether]] is "a form of existence of the matter, but it differs qualitatively from the common (atomic and molecular) substance or radiation (photons)".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://editura.mttlc.ro/iovitz-etherons.html?Lang=En|title=Ioan-Iovitz Popescu - Ether and Etherons. A Possible Reappraisal of the Concept of Ether (1982)}}</ref> The fluid aether is "governed by the principle of inertia and its presence produces a modification of the space-time geometry".<ref>{{Cite book|title=Etherons as predicted by Ioan-Iovitz Popescu in 1982|last=Duursma|first=Egbert|publisher=CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform|year=2015|isbn=978-1511906371}}</ref> Built upon Le Sage's ultra-mundane corpuscles, Popescu's theory posits a finite Universe "filled with some particles of exceedingly small mass (of about 10<sup>−69</sup> kg), traveling chaotically at speed of light" and material bodies "made up of such particles called etherons".<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Worldwide List of Alternative Theories and Critics. Formerly: The Worldwide List of Dissidents Scientists|last=de Climont|first=Jean|date=November 2020 |publisher=Editions d Assailly |isbn=978-2902425174}}</ref>

In recent years, the interest of Iovitzu Popescu has shifted to the field of [[quantitative linguistics]],<ref>{{Cite book |title=Word Frequency Studies |last1=Popescu |first1=Ioan-Iovitz |last2=Altmann |first2=Gabriel |last3=Gryzbek |first3=Peter |last4=Jayaram |first4=Bijapur D. |last5=Köhler |first5=Reinhard |last6=Krupa |first6=Victor |last7=Macutek |first7=Ján |last8=Pustet |first8=Regina |last9=Uhlirová |first9=Ludmila |last10=Vidya |first10=Matummal N. |publisher=De Gruyter Mouton |year=2009 |isbn=978-3-11-021852-7 |location=Berlin, New York |display-authors=1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Quantitative Analysis of Poetic Texts |last1=Popescu |first1=Ioan-Iovitz |last2=Lupea |first2=Mihaiela |last3=Tatar |first3=Doina |last4=Altmann |first4=Gabriel |publisher=De Gruyter Mouton |year=2015 |isbn=978-3-11-036379-1 |location=Berlin, Boston}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rrp.infim.ro/2008_60_3/03-417-422.pdf?Lang=En|title=On the symbiosis of physicists and linguists|access-date=2022-08-14|archive-date=2022-10-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221017222636/http://www.rrp.infim.ro/2008_60_3/03-417-422.pdf?Lang=En|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://editura.mttlc.ro/FW-mathematics.html?Lang=En|title=''Finnegans Wake'' Seen from the Angle of Mathematics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://editura.mttlc.ro/iovitz-wilson-lambda.html?Lang=En|title=Andrew Wilson & Ioan–Iovitz Popescu - Vocabulary Richness in English Poetry: The Lambda Indicator and Beyond}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.geocities.ws/iipopescu/6_Text_ranking_by_the_weight_of_highly_frequent_words.pdf Popescu, Text ranking by the weight of highly frequent words, pp 557 - 567 (2007)}}</ref> which has become one of his favorite leisure activities. His main collaborator in this field was [[Gabriel Altmann]] from [[Ruhr University Bochum]].

The career achievements of Popescu have been recognized and celebrated by various personalities<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iipopescu.com/Iovitzu_at_80_as_seen_by_Dr._George_Dinescu.pdf?Lang=En|title=Ioan-Iovitz Popescu as seen by Dr. Gheorghe Dinescu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rrp.infim.ro/2008_60_3/01-407-411.pdf?Lang=En|title=Iovitzu seen by Nicholas Ionescu-Pallas|access-date=2022-08-15|archive-date=2022-08-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815184905/http://www.rrp.infim.ro/2008_60_3/01-407-411.pdf?Lang=En|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://rrp.infim.ro/2008_60_3/02-413-415.pdf?Lang=En|title=Life and scientific works of Ioan-Iovitz Popescu at the 75 year anniversary|access-date=2022-08-15|archive-date=2022-08-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815184852/http://rrp.infim.ro/2008_60_3/02-413-415.pdf?Lang=En|url-status=dead}}</ref> and organizations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iipopescu.com/OPERA_OMNIA_2009_Award_to_Ioan_Iovitz_Popescu.pdf?Lang=En|title=Ioan-Iovitz Popescu: Opera Omnia}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acad.ro/com2017/pag_com17_1006.htm?Lang=En|title=Romanian Academy - Anniversary Session - Acad. Ioan Iovitz Popescu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.caleaeuropeana.ro/personalitati-ale-romaniei-premiate-la-a-ii-a-editie-a-galei-premiilor-marii-loji/?Lang=En|title=Romanian personalities honored at the 2nd edition of the National Grand Lodge Awards|date=23 June 2012 }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Iovitzu Popescu was married to Denisa-Georgeta Popescu from 1963 until her death in 2003. Together they co-authored 35 papers on optogalvanic and laser spectroscopy. The author biography of Iovitzu Popescu was published in 2020, titled "Iovițu's life".<ref>{{Cite book |title=Iovițu's Life |last=Popescu |first=Ioan-Iovitz |publisher=The Publishing House of the Romanian Academy |year=2020 |isbn=978-973-27-3516-9 |location=Bucharest, Romania}}</ref> He died on 22 December 2023 at the age of 91.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miclea |first=Ioan |date=2023-12-22 |title=In memoriam acad. Ioan-Ioviț Popescu, rector al Universității din București în perioada 1981-1988 |url=https://unibuc.ro/in-memoriam-acad-ioan-iovit-popescu-rector-al-universitatii-din-bucuresti-in-perioada-1981-1988/ |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=UniBuc - Universitatea din București |language=ro-RO}}</ref>

== Awards ==
{{No sources|section|date= July 2025}}
The excellence of Iovitzu Popescu's work has been widely recognized:
* 1961 - Physics Prize, awarded by the [[Ministry of National Education (Romania)|Ministry of National Education]].
* 1966 - "[[Constantin Miculescu]]" prize for Physics awarded by the [[Romanian Academy]].
* 1997 - Honorary Citizen of [[Mehedinți County]].
* 1998 - Doctor Honoris Causa of the [[University of Craiova]].
* 2000 - Commander of the [[Order of Faithful Service]] awarded by the [[President of Romania]].
* 2002 - "Meritul Academic" diploma awarded by the Romanian Academy.
* 2002 - "Diploma of Excellence" awarded by the [[Ministry of National Education (Romania)|Ministry of Education and Research]].
* 2009 - "Opera Omnia" prize for lifetime achievements in science awarded by [[National University Research Council|CNCSIS]].
* 2009 - "Diploma of Excellence" of [[Drobeta-Turnu Severin]] City.
* 2010 - "Medal of Honor" awarded by the Institute of Atomic Physics.
* 2012 - "Grigore Moisil" award for exact sciences awarded by the National Grand Lodge of Romania.
* 2012 - "Diploma of Excellence" awarded by the Ministry of Education and Research.

== Bibliography ==
To date, the most cited peer-reviewed publication of Iovitzu Popescu remains his collaborative review, with Silviu Olariu, on the quantum effects of electromagnetic fluxes,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Olariu |first1=S. |last2=Popescu |first2=I. Iovitzu |date=1985 |title=The quantum effects of electromagnetic fluxes |journal=[[Reviews of Modern Physics]] |volume=57 |issue=2 |pages=339–436 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.57.339|bibcode=1985RvMP...57..339O }}</ref> recently quoted in the review paper Topological Metamaterials (2022).<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Ni |first1=Xiang |last2=Yves |first2=Simon |last3=Krasnok |first3=Alex |last4=Alu |first4=Andrea |date=2022 |title=Topological Metamaterials |class=physics.optics |eprint=2211.10006}}</ref>

Popescu's handwritten textbook on [[geometrical optics]], first published in 1988, was recently translated into English and is freely available online.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Optics. I. Geometrical Optics |last=Popescu |first=Ioan–Ioviț |publisher=Contemporary Literature Press |year=2017 |isbn=978-606-760-105-3 |url=http://editura.mttlc.ro/iovitz-optics.html }}</ref>

His most notable books and scientific publications are:<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=iqhVvzEAAAAJ |title=Ioan Iovitz Popescu - Google Scholar Citations |website=scholar.google.com |access-date=2022-08-15 |archive-date=2022-04-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220426181835/https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=iqhVvzEAAAAJ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* ''The quantum effects of electromagnetic fluxes ''
* ''Word frequency studies ''
* ''Accelerated emission of gamma rays from the 31-yr isomer of 178 Hf induced by X-Ray irradiation ''
* ''The coherent and incoherent pumping of a gamma ray laser with intense optical radiation ''
* ''Use of space-charge-amplification techniques in the absorption spectroscopy of Cs and Cs 2 ''
* ''Multiphoton excitation and ionization of atomic cesium with a tunable dye laser ''
* ''Multiphoton ionization of cesium through resonant dissociative states of Cs2 ''
* ''Aspects of word frequencies ''
